items.title: 3 Major Updates: Databricks Intelligent Document Processing
items.author: Advancing Analytics
items.summary:
Getting Intelligent Document Processing (IDP) into production is one thing. Making it scalable, cost-effective and compliant? That's where things get interesting.

Databricks has rolled out three updates that tackle some of the practical challenges of enterprise IDP, and Gavi, our Chief AI Officer, is joined by Sepi, AI product Specialist at Databricks, to break them down.

They walk through the new document parsing task in Lakeflow Jobs, which makes ingesting and processing documents at scale much simpler. Then there's AI Gateway, where new budget controls give teams a better handle on AI spending. And finally, expanded UK South support for AI functions, an important step for organisations navigating data residency requirements.

This essentially means there'll be less friction getting documents into your pipelines, more control over what you're spending, and greater flexibility over where your data is processed. All good news for anyone trying to make IDP work in the real world.

In this video you'll learn:

- How to deploy Intelligent Document Processing using the new document parsing task in Databricks Lakeflow Jobs
- How to automate document ingestion using connectors for SharePoint, Google Drive, Salesforce and more
- How to set budgets for Databricks AI functions using AI Gateway
- How AI Gateway helps organisations monitor and control AI spending across teams and projects
- What UK South regional support means for AI Parse, AI Extract, AI Classify and AI Decide
- Why regional AI processing matters for data residency, compliance and regulated industries

items.title: Hemut built an AI operating system for trucking carriers using Confluent Cloud
items.author: Confluent, an IBM Company
items.summary:
Hemut provides an AI operating system for carriers and brokers, combining a full ERP and TMS into a platform where much of the work runs itself. This powers the Internet of Freight, where fleets operate on a connected network that allows efficiency gains to compound and benefit everyone the industry touches, including carriers whose costs fall, drivers who get paid faster, and consumers who pay less for the goods trucks deliver.

But none of that works if the underlying picture of the business is not current. An AI system acting on stale information can make matters worse rather than better. That is why Hemut built a real-time data foundation for its platform with Confluent Cloud.

items.title: He Used 100 Billion Tokens in a Month - Waymo Talks
items.author: AAIF Live
items.summary:
What happens when your AI coding agent gets better at finding bugs - but never knows when to stop?

Jesse Vincent, creator of Superpowers and founder of Prime Radiant, joins us to explore what it actually takes to get useful work out of AI agents.

We start with a tiny Playdate game console turned into a voice-controlled client for his coding agent. Then we dig into why agents ignore skills, what goes wrong when code review becomes an endless loop, and Jesse’s experience using 100 billion tokens in a month - including turning 30 years of email into a searchable personal knowledge base.

Jesse also walks through his custom coding agent, Evener, his approach to preserving context, and why asking an agent for a video proving its work can reveal what tests miss.

Finally, we explore AI colleagues with ongoing jobs: project managers and developers that coordinate work, ship fixes, and run postmortems.

If you use Claude Code, Codex, Superpowers, or other AI coding tools, this conversation offers practical ideas for moving from generated code to software you can actually ship.
